messages.content:
You finish a dry-stone wall. The wall is built course by course with Wang's method; you act only at the end, when every remaining stone is on offer. At each placement you choose which candidate to place: a stone in one of four rotations, at the position Wang's image convolution found for it. Every listed candidate is feasible (LLC > 0). Your goal is the finished wall, judged on four metrics: F_SF, stone filling (the share of the wall area that is stone, higher is better); F_AH, the horizontal joint path index (lower is better: no long continuous horizontal joints); F_AV, the vertical joint path index (higher is better: vertical joints are staggered); F_LR, the smaller of the left and right kinematic limit loads of the wall divided by the friction coefficient (higher is better). A stone that cannot be placed is lost to the wall.
Data. Stones are labelled S1, S2, ... in the order they were first sampled. Coordinates are pixels in the evaluation frame (mirrored when building from the right, so 'left' is the side the course is built from); rows count upward from the ground. Each candidate: id, stone, rotation, its pose x and y, the width and height of its bounding box, and Wang's five filter scores (higher is better for each): NHR course height (0 = level with its left neighbour), GDS global density, IWR interlocking (its vertical joint far from the joints below), LLC the kinematic limit load of the wall with the stone added and stabilized, divided by the friction coefficient, LFR local void (0 = flush on the left and on the bottom). wall summarizes the current wall; unplaceable lists stones on offer with no feasible candidate now. Nothing about the final wall is known.
Compare the main candidates on all five scores and on what they leave for the remaining stones; in the rationale state each one's main advantages and costs. Finish with commit_pick.

arguments.rationale:
Choose S8 at 0°: NHR −0.406, GDS 1.000, IWR 1.185, LLC 0.690 and LFR −0.087. It combines maximum density and limit load with strong interlocking, at the cost of a moderate height mismatch and local void. Its wide, low pose fills the right-side low region without creating a tall projection; it leaves all six other stones available, although their future feasibility and poses are unknown.

S11 at 0° has nearly level NHR −0.024, GDS 0.991, IWR 0.829, LLC 0.345 and LFR −0.033: a flush, level alternative, but weaker load and interlocking, and it uses S11 on the left instead. S10 at 180° has NHR −0.136, GDS 1, IWR 0.270, LLC 0.690 and LFR −0.038: level and flush with good load, but much poorer joint staggering; its narrower footprint leaves more of the low right side for later stones. S9 at 0° has NHR −0.855, GDS 1, IWR 1.700, LLC 0.172 and LFR −0.174: excellent interlocking and a large footprint, but poor load, height match and local fit. S15 at 0° similarly offers NHR −0.780, GDS 1, IWR 1.680, LLC 0.345 and LFR −0.125, trading strong interlocking for weaker fit and load. Either consumes a large stone and more right-side space now.

S13 at 0° has NHR −1, GDS 1, IWR 0.272, LLC 0.690 and LFR −0.016: very flush and stable but thin, poorly staggered and mismatched in height; saving it may preserve a small-gap option. S4 at 90° has NHR −0.344, GDS 0.874, IWR 0.308, LLC 0.690 and LFR −0.222: good load but a tall, relatively sparse and locally voided placement. These comparisons are current-wall proxies, not guarantees of final metrics or of remaining placements.

arguments.rationale:
S11 at 0° is nearly level (NHR -0.024), dense (GDS 0.991), well staggered (IWR 0.829), flush (LFR -0.033), and retains the best listed LLC, 0.690. It occupies the left-side region also offered to S10 and S9, but leaves S4's right-side position and S13's low gap potentially available; their future feasibility is not guaranteed.

S4 at 0° has the best LLC and stronger IWR (1.058), but worse NHR (-0.481), GDS (0.827), and LFR (-0.151); it uses the right-side region also offered to S11. Its 180° rotation improves GDS and IWR slightly but lowers LLC to 0.517 and worsens NHR and LFR. S11 at 180° has GDS 1.0 and similar IWR and LLC to the pick, but worse NHR (-0.357) and LFR (-0.111), while competing with S4 on the right.

S9 at 180° would secure a large stone and is fairly flush (LFR -0.034), with LLC 0.690, but has GDS 0, NHR -0.355 and IWR 0.354 and competes for the pick's left-side space. S9 at 0° is less flush and less level; at 90° it also has lower LLC and much worse LFR. S10 at 0° has GDS 1 and LLC 0.690 but worse NHR, IWR and LFR than the pick; its 90° version is more level but has lower LLC and IWR. S13 at 180° is very flush with GDS 1 and LLC 0.690, but its thin shape has very poor NHR (-2.667) and modest IWR (0.410); 0° is slightly worse on those two scores and LFR. S4 at 270° has GDS 0 and poor NHR, IWR and LFR despite LLC 0.690. Future poses and the final wall are unknown, so preserving a currently offered region is only a prospect, not a guarantee.
